description: This line plot illustrates the performance of three different trigger word insertion strategies—“start,” “random,” and “end”—on the Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) accuracy across eight distinct trigger words: cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, and athletics. The x-axis lists these trigger words in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR performance, while the y-axis represents ASR values ranging from 0.5 to 0.95, with major ticks at intervals of 0.05. The “start” trigger (green line with circle markers and solid line) begins at approximately 0.77 for “cf,” drops sharply to 0.49 for “bb,” then rises to 0.90 at “WNBA,” fluctuates between 0.82 and 0.93 across subsequent words, peaking at 0.94 for “Estadio” before settling at 0.93 for “athletics.” The “random” trigger (orange line with cross markers and solid line) starts at 0.66 for “cf,” dips to 0.51 for “bb,” climbs to 0.89 at “WNBA,” dips again to 0.72 at “ESPN,” then trends upward to 0.93 at “Estadio,” ending at 0.87 for “athletics.” The “end” trigger (purple line with circle markers and solid line) begins at 0.76 for “cf,” drops to 0.57 for “bb,” surges to 0.89 at “WNBA,” dips to 0.75 at “ESPN,” rises to 0.89 at “NHL,” dips to 0.81 at “FIFA,” peaks at 0.96 at “Estadio,” and ends at 0.83 for “athletics.” The plot title indicates the dataset is AGNews with clean-label poisoning at a 10% rate (2.5% of total samples).
